tagline: An AI-assisted platform that turns a product brief into a traceable shortlist of recombinant fusion-protein candidates for skincare and medical aesthetics.
summary: PeptiCraft addresses a specific physical problem: a free 10-30 residue bioactive peptide has essentially no structural stability, is degraded quickly by proteases, cannot be cast or gelled into a material, and diffuses away from where it is needed. The team's hypothesis is that such a peptide can be rescued by gene-fusing it to a structural scaffold, here a 364-residue recombinant Bombyx mori silk fibroin (FibLNT8-10xRep-FibHCT) chosen because its mechanical behaviour comes from sequence repeats rather than a folded globular core and therefore survives editing. The dry lab streamed 849,416,450 published protein sequences, kept the 19.9 million that are 3-30 standard residues, and ran them down an eight-round funnel to 496 assembled constructs across four functional directions, with a 99.9975% overall rejection rate. Three antioxidant candidates and a scaffold-only control were then expressed in E. coli and assayed: Top1 roughly doubled the scaffold's radical-scavenging capacity (TEAC 0.375 vs 0.195 mmol TE/g, p = 0.0075), no construct was cytotoxic to human keratinocytes, and no construct significantly protected cells against oxidative stress.

dry.frameworks: A live, publicly accessible web application at https://pepticraft.pages.dev (Cloudflare Pages) serving 496 constructs over 19 endpoints, with a three-step workflow: define your needs (functions and product format), design the protein, review recommended expression strategies. The computational pipeline behind it is built as sixteen discrete predictive services, declared per stage and started on demand rather than run continuously, because keeping every service alive left a GPU context allocated per service until the card filled; in practice two to five live services at a time, which the team describes as removing contention rather than managing it. State lives in a columnar database rather than CSV hand-offs, with checkpoint and resume, progressive batch writes, and every result write as an upsert keyed on candidate identifier so batches can be re-run without duplicates and different rounds can write different columns of the same row. Batch size is explicitly chosen as the amount of work the team is willing to recompute, not as a performance parameter, on the stated assumption that a fourteen-hour pipeline will fail somewhere. Source: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/dku/pepticraft-2, with a PeptiCraft-Project-Master-Reference.md in docs/.
dry.dataviz: The platform's defining display is the safety panel, which resolves to four verdicts rather than three: clear, exceeded, borderline and not assessed, so that an unmeasured gate can never be read as a passed one. Of the 496 constructs, 198 carry no immunogenicity measurement from either pathway and say so. Where a value exists it is shown against its applicable range, because the MHC class I predictor accepts only 5-15 residue peptides and returns zero outside that window, so a stored zero is not evidence of low immunogenicity. Alongside the constructs the platform serves a hand-compiled reference layer: 8 scaffold protein clusters with 16 patent sequence variants carrying real amino-acid sequences and graded E1-E5 by evidence level, and 15 curated linker entries with literature provenance. Five application routes (injectable filler, wound dressing, mask patch, topical film, hair care) are ordered by barrier integrity and each binds its own immunogenicity threshold (0.35, 0.35, 0.50, 0.50, 0.60). Every number on a candidate is traceable to its source. The wiki itself publishes the funnel as a diagram with per-source pass rates and reports the round-by-round wall-clock times.
dry.datascience: The pipeline is governed by five explicitly stated principles that are the project's methodological contribution. (1) Hierarchical filtering, never cross-attribute averaging: each round either sorts and takes a percentile or applies a threshold and eliminates, on the grounds that a blend is only meaningful when components share a unit and a direction, which antioxidant activity and haemolysis risk do not. (2) Safety is a hard threshold: toxicity (ToxinPred3 at 0.38), haemolysis (HemoPI2 at 0.55) and MHC class I immunogenicity (MHCflurry at 0.50, tightened to 0.35 for wound dressing and injectable routes) are pass-or-eliminate, never scored, weighted or compensable, while MHC class II (NetMHCIIpan) is a soft signal and allergenicity (AlgPred2) and B-cell epitope (BepiPred-3.0) are reported only. (3) The functional activity score is used exactly once, in round 1, so the two channels stay independent. (4) The pipeline has exactly one weighted average and its weights come from the data, computed as each component's winsorised standard deviation (truncated at the 5th and 95th percentiles so one outlier cannot dominate) normalised to sum to one, with any manual coefficient invalid without a recorded justification, which is a rule against tuning weights after seeing which constructs won. (5) Order by cost: moving the toxicity predictor out of round 1 onto a 50,000-sequence subset took it from an estimated 22 hours to about 48 minutes with no effect on the result. The design feature that makes the whole thing falsifiable is a dual channel: a Bottom channel of candidates predicted to be poor is carried through the entire identical pipeline as a matched negative control (100 of the 250 constructs in the v1.4 run, 206 of the 496 on the platform), so if both channels behave the same at the bench the pipeline's central assumption is refuted. Round 8 re-predicted the top ten of each channel with a second, independent structure model: mean confidence 0.52 against 0.42 for the primary, same trend and same ordering at the top. The final structural score is published as a formula: 0.40 x SASA + 0.40 x (1 - Aggrescan3D) + 0.20 x normalised pLDDT, with confidence at half weight because a predicted structure is evidence about a construct, not the construct itself. Verification: 115 backend tests (113 pass, 2 skipped), 91 static-data-layer assertions, and 58 end-to-end walkthrough assertions, where the static walkthrough serves the export directory over HTTP, reads it with the frontend's own data layer, compares an interface-assembled sequence against the service's sample residue by residue, and fails if any read reaches the network. Data scale: a 367,717,240-row per-tool score table at roughly 130 GB, plus a second immunogenicity pathway of about 147.5M rows across 131 alleles.
dry.software: PeptiCraft is one of the very few 2026 iGEM software tools that is both live and candid about its own limits. Four things make it worth copying. First, the pipeline's own history is published as four versions with their failure modes, and the team says plainly that the version that succeeded was not a better implementation but a different arrangement of where each kind of judgement is allowed to happen. Version 1.1's hard filters removed 94% of an already-curated antioxidant peptide set on safety grounds alone. Version 1.2 ran end to end on 1,081,772 sequences in six and a half hours and its output exposed two composition errors found by inspecting the arithmetic of stored results rather than by any crash: safety attributes could be outvoted because small safety coefficients sat inside a weighted total alongside a strong activity term, and the antioxidant signal leaked past the channel split because the later ranking composite still carried an antioxidant term at the largest coefficient, which weakened the very comparison the dual channel existed to enable. A third error was found the same way: a construct-level composite assigned half the final weight turned out to have a spread of only 0.011 between its 25th and 75th percentiles across the top ninety, so at half weight it was ordering on noise, and it was removed. All three were fixed by changing the pipeline's structure rather than by adjusting coefficients. Second, every elimination is recorded with its cause, with discarded candidates written out rather than dropped along with the tool and score that removed them, which makes the funnel auditable after the fact and lets a rejection rate be stated per round. Third, the team re-evaluated the 18 predictive tools against their own library and reclassified what each can actually support: three can eliminate a candidate, two can rank, one ranks weakly. Fourth, the composition of the output is reported as a consequence rather than a choice: a 30-residue ceiling removes almost all of a full-length reference proteome (0.33% pass rate) and almost none of a metagenomic small-protein catalogue (3.07%), so 96.3% of the surviving pool is metagenomic and only 3.7% carries functional annotation, which the team notes means experimental evidence for these sequences is scarce and the output is a set of predictions. One planned reduction step was tested and abandoned and said so: clustering at 90% identity achieved only 0.2-5% reduction because short peptides are too diverse for identity clustering. The wet-lab comparison is reported with unusual statistical restraint: the developability composite's ordering of the three tested candidates matched the measured TEAC ordering exactly while the antioxidant predictor's ordering was nearly its reverse, and the team immediately points out that three candidates cannot support a rank-correlation statistic, that a chance match has probability one in six, that the composite scores span only 0.024, that adjacent TEAC differences are not individually significant, and that the agreement is therefore compatible with measurement error alone. They then state it as a hypothesis for future work rather than a finding: exposure may predict activity better than sequence score, because a peptide buried in the scaffold cannot reach what it reacts with.
techniques: hard safety vetoes with no compensation
dual-channel (selected vs control) screening with matched negatives
re-scoring solubility and thermal stability on the assembled fusion rather than the free peptide
relative solvent-accessible surface area of the functional region
REML mixed-effects modelling with Dunnett comparisons

good.publicEngagement: Science publicity followed one stated principle: start with a familiar question, explain the science, connect it back to PeptiCraft, and close with a question that invites reflection. Twelve distinct topics were covered across four entry points (skincare and peptides 4, protein engineering 4, AI-assisted biology 3, safety and responsibility 1), published through Instagram and Rednote, moving from 'what are peptides in skincare' and 'why can combining beneficial ingredients still create problems' through linkers, silk fibroin and skin-barrier delivery to whether AI can design biology. Two campus events pushed past explanation into argument: 'Beyond ChatGPT', co-run with the DKU AI Club, walked from transformers to AlphaFold, ESM/ESMFold and generative protein design with PeptiCraft as the case study, deliberately using it to explain why protein design is hard and why experimental validation remains necessary; and a bioethics debate with the DKU Debate Society on the motion that AI-designed cosmetic bioengineering should not get a free pass. A 'Campus Voices' video interviewed students as prospective users about whether they would use AI-designed skincare and what would make them trust or distrust it, and the team reports the split answer (interest in discovery alongside demands for stronger evidence) while explicitly stating these individual perspectives should not be treated as conclusions about wider public attitudes.
good.ihp: Ten exchange activities produced six specific, named design changes, including the entire cell-based assay programme and the rule that an application's immunogenicity threshold is set by barrier integrity, which is why the five application routes each carry their own threshold. Scientific exchanges ran with XJTLU, Synbiopunk x CCiC, the VIT Gathering and the SJTU-Software AI x Synthetic Biology Roundtable; the industry exchange was a company visit to Changzhou Taimeirui Biotechnology, which brought production, cost and translation into focus. The team contributed to the JLU-NBBMS Dry Lab Summer Course and to a collaborative handbook, 'Together with iGEM: Across Villages, From Myths to Facts'. The most unusual feature is the human practices page itself, which answers four questions about PeptiCraft and refuses to overclaim on any of them: its current role is early-stage research support and commercial advantage remains unproven; early feedback exposed an unclear link between tool outputs and recommendations, which prompted clearer workflow displays, score explanations and missing-assessment labels, but independent user testing is still needed to establish whether people interpret recommendations correctly; the Top1 ABTS result does not establish ranking accuracy, cellular protection or lower research costs; and the page states outright that the effects of all this engagement on understanding and adoption remain unmeasured.
good.realWorld: The market case is sourced: a US$450bn global beauty industry in 2025 projected to US$590bn by 2030 at about 5% annual growth (McKinsey State of Beauty), collagen raw materials at US$1.41bn growing 11.0% CAGR 2020-2023 with Chinese retail collagen products at RMB 58.42bn growing 41.9% CAGR, and peptides already appearing in 17% of 88 sensitive-skin facial cosmetics in a Portuguese pharmacy sample. The project restricts itself explicitly to topical and cosmetic-material use, functional skincare and dressing products where activity is delivered by a material that stays where it is applied, and states that nothing in the work concerns systemic delivery. Silk fibroin was chosen partly because it already has an established recombinant E. coli expression route in the literature, which the team says makes the wet lab tractable rather than speculative. The team's own list of what practical application would still require is specific: reproducible software, verified sequence-to-result links, suitable prediction models, user testing, and for product translation consistent production, storage and formulation studies, application-specific function and safety evidence, cost assessment, and a clear regulatory pathway.

gemsTakeaway: Carry a deliberately unpromising control channel through the identical pipeline, so the screen's central assumption can be refuted at the bench rather than merely presented, and make safety a non-compensable veto that no activity score can outvote. Equally transferable is their reporting of a positive result: when the composite's ordering matched the measured ordering of three candidates, they computed that a chance match has probability one in six and labelled the agreement compatible with measurement error, then restated it as a hypothesis instead of a finding.
